newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses climb, ignoring unsteady Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses climb, ignoring unsteady Wall St.

text.p: European bourses moved ahead on Tuesday shrugging off an unsteady opening by Wall Street which appeared to mark the end of its record-breaking run.
On currency markets, the dollar recovered from two-month lows against the mark on supportive remarks by Bundesbank council members.

Frankfurt was the strongest performer, climbing to a record intra-day high on the IBIS DAX index in computerised transactions as the dollar strengthened, offering improved potential for German exporters.
The 30-share IBIS DAX jumped 32.18 points to an all-time high of 2,762.62 points before slipping back slightly. The previous best was set only last Friday. Floor trading ended up slightly.

In Amsterdam, Dutch shares ended at a fresh closing high, the second in two days, but well short of a new intra-day high after coming close to breaking through the 600 level on AEX share index for the first time.
The index closed 0.49 points higher at 597.59, after climbing to 599.69 in the opening hours of the session, buoyed by another record high closing overnight on Wall Street.

In London, stocks built up a head of steam in early trading drawing strength from Wall Street's fourth consecutive record close on Monday. The momentum kept London ahead, even when Wall Street opened in the minus column on Tuesday.

The London bourse was registering gains of 0.4 percent in mid-afternoon but with trading levels still relatively low, some said the index would struggle to push much higher in the short term against a background of fears of rising British interest rates.
"Wall Street has dragged us up on its coat-tails but it is very hard work and we are struggling to go forward," said one sales trader.
The strong showing in Europe came despite the disappointing start on Wall Street which had its fourth consecutive record close on Monday.
The Dow Jones average's latest bull run is the biggest boom since a seven-session record streak in February. Last week's 198-point post-election rally was the second-biggest weekly point gain ever.
French stocks recovered their composure after slipping in early trade to show a gain of over one percent after comments by a Bundesbank official on the U.S. currency.

Bundesbank directorate member Edgar Meister said the current dollar exchange rate was "not appropriate". The dollar rose, which heartened French investors as dollar strength could help U.S. appetite for foreign assets.

Meister's comments, coupled with remarks by Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp that he believed a stronger dollar might be more appropriate, helped the dollar recover from lows against the mark.
The U.S. currency was keeping to narrow ranges below 1.50 marks in late European trade after the Bundesbank comments propelled it briefly above these levels.
Currency analysts said with a full schedule of Bundesbank officials speaking over the next three days, these comments could be the start of a fresh round of verbal dollar support.
"Clearly what we're seeing is the Bundesbank go into a strategy of verbal support for the dollar," said James McKay, international economist at PaineWebber in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4995 marks and 111.30 yen, compared with 1.4983 marks and 111.20 yen in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1600 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 19.0 points higher at 3,933.4.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 5.98 points at 2,734.30.
PARIS - The CAC 40 index was up 23.93 points at 2229.13
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1220 GMT
Gold was fixed at $381.90 an ounce in the afternoon, compared with $380.75 at the close on Monday. Silver was higher at $4.88, up one two cent.
